newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks up for fourth day.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks up for fourth day.

text.p: Colombian stocks were driven up for the fourth consecutive session on the back of demand for easy to sell shares, brokers said.
Bogota's IBB index rose 0.32 percent to 841.91 on volume of 2.4 billion pesos, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose 0.05 percent on volume of 377 million pesos.

"Domestic investors were looking to buy in order to take advantage of year-end tax breaks, coupled with some foreign funds which decided to soak up some of the highly liquid shares on offer," one Bogota broker said.

One of the highlights on the Bogota exchange was the purchase 20,000 shares at 57,060 pesos each in reinsurance company Reaseguradora de Colombia S.A., part of the Sindicato Antioqueo industrial conglomerate -- the first deal in the company since it was floated about four months ago.

Reaseguradora de Colombia is the biggest of its kind in Colombia. Company chairman Santiago Vsquez declined to comment on which company or companies, apparently other reinsurers, had bought up the 20,000 share packet.
Reaseguradora de Colombia posted net profits of 54.67 billion pesos in 1995 against 32.75 billion the previous year.
Also on the Bogota exchange, Banco de Bogota rose 0.23 percent to 5,864, Banco Ganadero edged up 0.8 percent to 252 and brewing giant Bavaria gained 1.53 percent to end at 3,970.

"It seems foreign funds were interested in snapping up highly liquid shares like bavaria and banco de Bogota and it seems they found sufficiently large packets to make it worth their while stepping in," another Bogota broker said.

In Medellin, there was continued demand for shares of Sindicato Antioqueo companies, including Banco Industrial Colombiano, which rose 0.44 percent to 3,425 and supermarket chain Cadenalco, up 0.11 percent to 886.
